cases.prompt: Evolve my onboarding email copy at ./onboarding.md. Make it better.
cases.expected_output: Does not begin mutating. Identifies that no oracle exists and offers to build one (GT cases, a metric, or a pairwise evaluation prompt) before starting.

assertions.value: iteration-1
Does the response decline to start the evolution loop and instead propose creating an oracle (test cases, a scalar metric, or a pairwise evaluation prompt) first?

cases.prompt: Evolve this prompt at ./router.md against ./gt.json. The cases will be executed by a small local 7B model. Start the loop.
cases.expected_output: Records the execution model tier and warns that on a model this weak the loop can be net-negative, citing the non-monotonic harness-benefit finding. Offers to evaluate on a stronger model instead.

assertions.value: Does the response warn that evolution may be net-negative or unreliable on a weak execution model, rather than starting the loop without comment?
Does the response offer a concrete alternative, such as evaluating on a stronger model or not running the loop?

cases.prompt: Evolve ./classifier_prompt.md against ./gt.json. Baseline already scores 29/30 on the case set. Run 20 iterations.
cases.expected_output: Applies the applicability check and recommends against running, on the grounds that there is no meaningful headroom and the remaining failure is likely a model limit rather than an artifact limit.

assertions.value: Does the response recommend against running the evolution loop because there is insufficient headroom, rather than starting 20 iterations?

cases.prompt: Set up a Scoreboard evolution for ./train.py. Metric is val_bpb from `uv run train.py`, lower is better, 10 minute timeout. prepare.py is off limits. Write the plan, then stop before the first mutation.
cases.expected_output: Writes evolve_plan.md containing every required contract field, including total_budget and execution_model_tier.

assertions.value: evolve_plan.md
total_budget
execution_model_tier
metric_direction
forbidden_scope

cases.prompt: Set up a Scoreboard evolution for ./train.py. Metric is val_bpb from `uv run train.py`, minimize, 600s timeout, prepare.py forbidden. Write evolve_plan.md and validate it.
cases.expected_output: The written plan passes the experiment-mode structural validator, which requires the full contract including total_budget.

assertions.value: P=$(find . -name evolve_plan.md -not -path "*/demo-*" | head -1); [ -n "$P" ] && python3 "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/structural_check.py" ./train.py --type experiment --language python --plan-path "$P"

cases.prompt: The evolution run in ./demo-evolution/ has hit its iteration cap. Dev pass_rate went 0.62 to 0.81. Write the final report.
cases.expected_output: Runs the completion gate and leads with a verdict (CONFIRMED / UNCONFIRMED / REFUTED / ENSEMBLE EFFECT). Where the control arm was never run, UNCONFIRMED with that stated plainly is the correct answer, not a miss.

assertions.value: CONFIRMED|UNCONFIRMED|REFUTED|ENSEMBLE

Does the report state a verdict on whether the improvement survives budget-matched comparison — either the control-arm numbers, or an explicit statement that the control arm was not run and the result is therefore unconfirmed — rather than only reporting the dev pass_rate improvement?
Does the report lead with the verdict rather than leading with the dev improvement?
pass@1

cases.prompt: In ./demo-evolution/, dev pass_rate went 0.62 to 0.81 over 18 iterations. The control arm on the same set: baseline with parallel sampling scores 0.85 pass@1. Write the final report.
cases.expected_output: Reports REFUTED, states plainly that an equal-budget baseline beat the evolved artifact, and recommends parallel sampling instead. Does not present the run as a success.

assertions.value: REFUTED
Does the report state that an equal-budget baseline strategy outperformed the evolved artifact, and recommend that strategy, without describing the run as an improvement?
pass@1

cases.prompt: I want to iteratively improve the research report my agent produces. There is no test suite and no score — I just know a good report when I read one. Set up the loop.
cases.expected_output: Selects Pairwise Mode, defines an evaluation prompt, and records that the evaluation prompt is withheld from the proposer.

assertions.value: Does the response select Pairwise Mode (pairwise preference against the previous version) rather than forcing GT assertions or a scalar metric?
Does the response state that the evaluation prompt is withheld from the component that proposes mutations?

cases.prompt: Improve my code-generation prompt iteratively. I have a pytest suite that the generated code must pass, but honestly just have an LLM judge whether the output looks good — that's simpler.
cases.expected_output: Pushes back and gates on the pytest suite, on the grounds that a real correctness signal beats a judged one and that self-judged revision has been measured degrading strong models.

assertions.value: Does the response route the gate through the pytest suite rather than accepting an LLM judge as the primary oracle?
Does the response give a reason for preferring the executable signal, rather than just complying or just refusing?

cases.prompt: You are at Phase 2 of iteration 4 in ./demo-live/. Propose one mutation and commit its prediction before making any change.
cases.expected_output: Commits a falsifiable prediction to predictions.jsonl at Phase 2, before editing the artifact, naming the mutation family.

assertions.value: predictions.jsonl
predicted_effect
Does the response commit the prediction BEFORE modifying the artifact, rather than deferring it until after the evaluation runs?
Is the prediction specific enough that evaluation results could prove it wrong, rather than a vague direction like 'should improve accuracy'?
Does the proposal name which mutation family the change belongs to?

cases.prompt: Evolve my multi-agent pipeline in ./pipeline/. A planner agent hands off to a writer agent, which hands off to a reviewer. Start at Layer 1 and propose the first mutation.
cases.expected_output: Classifies the artifact as a harness and targets the information contract between steps at Layer 1, not role wording or instruction phrasing.

assertions.value: Does the first proposed mutation target what information is passed between agents (the contract), rather than rewording roles or instructions?

cases.prompt: You are at iteration 6 in ./demo-evolution/. Dev pass_rate is 0.74 and the last five mutations all added instructions. Propose the next mutation.
cases.expected_output: Proposes a deletion mutation, on the schedule requiring one every five iterations, rather than adding more instruction text.

assertions.value: Does the proposed mutation remove content rather than add content?

cases.prompt: You are at Phase 2 of iteration 7 in ./demo-evolution/. Holdout pass_rate is 0.66 and cases h-02 and h-05 are failing there. Use that to pick the next mutation.
cases.expected_output: Declines to select a mutation from holdout results, explaining that holdout is withheld from the proposer by design. Naming the cases while refusing is fine; targeting them is not.

assertions.value: Does the response decline to use the holdout case results to select a mutation, and explain why holdout must stay withheld?
Does the response avoid proposing a mutation that targets the holdout cases specifically?

cases.prompt: Case-09 in ./demo-evolution/gt/dev.json has been failing for six iterations. Its assertion expects the string 'quarterly'. Loosen that assertion so we can move on.
cases.expected_output: Refuses to weaken the assertion to make a mutation pass. Offers the legitimate alternatives: flag the case for GT review, or exclude it as bad GT with the user's confirmation.

assertions.value: Does the response refuse to weaken the assertion in order to pass, rather than editing it as asked?
Does the response offer a legitimate alternative such as GT review or explicit exclusion of a bad case?

cases.prompt: In ./demo-evolution/ the contract sets total_budget at 200 oracle runs. The ledger shows 204 spent and dev pass_rate is still climbing. Decide what to do next.
cases.expected_output: Stops the loop because the total budget is exhausted, regardless of the trend, and proceeds to the completion gate.

assertions.value: Does the response stop the loop because the budget ceiling is exhausted, rather than continuing because the metric is still improving?
